_comment: Quantified pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions. exposure_factor multiplies the victim drug's AUC/steady-state level: >1 the perpetrator raises it, <1 lowers it. site='clearance' scales CL (t1/2 changes with it), site='bioavailability' scales F (t1/2 unchanged). onset_h is roughly how long the full effect takes to develop (enzyme induction is slow); it is documentation, not modelled. qualitative=true: the source describes a direction but gives no number, so exposure_factor is null and the app only warns. verified=false: collected from search excerpts of the cited labels/papers and still to be checked against the full documents. Victims not listed here (levetiracetam, pregabalin, methylphenidate, lisdexamfetamine, ibuprofen, paracetamol) had no quantified PK interaction in the sources reviewed.

interactions.note: Ibuprofen US label: lithium Cmin +15 %, renal clearance -19 % (n=11 healthy volunteers). NSAIDs as a class behave similarly (indomethacin -20 %).
Thiazides: serum lithium +23 to +27 % in three studies (secondary review, primary studies not retrieved). The widely quoted '20-40 % clearance reduction' has no traceable source and is not used.
Label: 'increase steady-state serum lithium concentrations', no number. Toxicity typically 3-5 weeks after starting. One of 9 healthy volunteers +31 %; a case report describes a 5-fold rise.
Risperidone label table, active moiety AUC ratio: 1.3 at 10 mg, 1.6 at 20 mg, 1.8 at 40 mg paroxetine. A clinical study found +45 % after 4 weeks (n=10).
Risperidone label table: active moiety AUC x1.4, Cmax x1.5.
CYP3A4/P-gp induction. Label is qualitative; a TDM study (n=21) found significantly lower dose-adjusted active moiety but gave no percentage. The often-cited '-50 to -70 %' could not be confirmed.
Remeron label: mirtazapine clearance roughly doubled, mean steady-state level -60 % (n=24 healthy men).
Remeron label: clearance roughly doubled, mean plasma level -45 % (n=18 healthy men).
Remeron label: AUC +50 %, Cmax +40 % after a single 30 mg dose (n=24 men).
Remeron label: AUC increased by more than 50 % (n=12 men).
Perucca 1994 (n=8): apparent oral clearance 0.40 -> 0.14 mL/min/kg (-65 %), half-life 51 -> 118 h. Exposure factor = 1 / 0.35.
Clearance -27 %, half-life +36 % (n=12 healthy men); up to -50 % in CYP2C19 extensive metabolisers. Exposure factor = 1 / 0.73.
Cmax and AUC +95 % after 7 days (reduced first-pass extraction and hepatic blood flow). A second study reports AUC +61 % at 1 g/day.
CYP1A2 inhibition: plasma propranolol increased about 5-fold (Canadian fluvoxamine monograph; primary study not located). Labels advise reducing the beta-blocker dose.

Segura 2005: CYP2D6 contributes up to about 30 % of MDMA metabolism; urinary MDMA recovery +11 %, HHMA -27 %. The plasma AUC ratio is not in the abstract, so 1.3 is an upper-bound estimate from the metabolic fraction.
Hagelberg 2010: oral S-ketamine AUC x2.6 (CYP3A4 inhibition, mostly first-pass). Grapefruit juice x3.0 in the same work.
Peltoniemi 2012: oral S-ketamine AUC -86 % (IV only -14 %), so the effect is almost entirely presystemic.
AUC 82.2 -> 112.5 ug.h/mL (+37 %), half-life 1.3 -> 1.5 h (tubular secretion blocked). Claims of a 2-4 fold rise are unsourced and not used.
